Your work is not clutter

Keep the context.
Question the cleanup.

The repository, the conversation and the credentials behind a project are not interchangeable with generated output.

The boundary

Known working state stays distinct.

.git

Source-control history

Repositories and their history are distinct from specific generated folders inside a project.

Sessions

Coding conversations

Known Codex, Claude Code and editor working locations are protected. A new or unfamiliar location still needs care.

Credentials

Access & recovery

Keychains, SSH keys, credential stores and recovery data belong outside routine cleanup.

Personal data

System & app-managed libraries

Mail, Messages, Photos, iCloud and system paths have protection boundaries. Some reviews send you to the owning app instead.

Before an action

Checks belong at the point of change.

Path

Inspect the real path

Normal cleanup checks the supplied path and its resolved location, including protected folders and symbolic-link boundaries.

Identity

Check the current item

The normal cleanup executor rechecks an item before moving it and verifies the recorded Trash destination. Changed or uncertain items must not be treated as the scanned candidate.

Outcome

Keep a record

Actions and failures are recorded. An uncertain result calls for inspection, not an automatic repeat of a destructive operation.

What this does not mean

Protection is not a backup.

Rules are based on known locations and evidence available to the scanner. Cairn cannot know the value of every file on your Mac. A folder called build is not enough on its own to establish that its contents are disposable.

Incomplete results may mean access was denied, a time limit was reached or a scan was stopped. Review the coverage before choosing an action.

Direct deletion cannot be undone through Cairn. Put Back depends on a matching recorded item still being in Trash. Keep independent backups of important work.

Get recovery guidance ↗
Release validation is still open.

These safeguards describe the normal cleanup implementation, not a guarantee across every experimental feature. Scheduled-rule consent, local-model removal, Apple Intelligence cancellation and broad Ruby gem cleanup require further safety work before release. Signing, notarisation and supported-Mac testing also remain outstanding.
